For any GM's out there who want to hit specific body parts, I created this - Tabletop RPGs

I'm about to start dming a campaign, and I want my players to be able to dismember, at the same time the semi official localized damage system in dnd SUCKS. So I created my own. Each body part will have its own health pool (each limb's health pool is 10% of total creature, torso is 30%, head and neck is 30%). Damage done to a section is half the attacks damage, if one area is reduced to zero, its severed. With the head, its an instant kill, and torso results in punctured lungs, which gives the creature exhausted status. Still tweaking, but its a decent base system, I think.

The DM from one of the games I'm playing in has asked me to clarify the use of this table. It is not to be used to determine which parts of your DM to cut off if they won't let you roll of the d10000 random effects table as a wild magic sorcerer (not that I would ever threaten him with that possibility due to my desire for chaos, I wonder where he got the idea that his limbs were at risk?)
Not bad, it can have its uses, but I will always use the Critical Hit Effects chart from the D&D 3/3.5 DMG if I want to have dismemberment.
Why do you have two 6's and 7's on the individual torso parts? Other than that, cool idea.

Why do you have two 6's and 7's on the individual torso parts?

Because that's roughly the middle of the body (I used to have it a bit further down, but a mistake in my math pushed it up), so will be hit by attacks aimed at the upper or lower half (it is a pretty large section, after all)...

What do you call torso? 6,7, and lower 8,9,10,11 would be my guess not sure if you are including lower 20 as well. If this is right upper body is the advantage to hit as there are 2 spots with 30% vs lower where there are 6, on the upper due to neck face head being shared on both sides they have 30% but are twice as likely as anything except the gonads to be hit so in reality are more like 15%. The results are Upper body 10 spots (arms) with 10%, 3 spots (head) 15%, 2 spots (torso) 30%, total 205 - Lower Body 1 spot (gonads) 5%, 8 spots (legs) 10%, 6 spots (torso) 30%, Total 265. I fully admit that this is a hard call statistically you have an advantage to the upper body having 60% less hitpoints to dismember but lower you will force the DM at some point to say you cut off someone's gonads.

Also you would need a chart for things that walk on 4 legs not just humans, and there are some things that your players just won't be dismembering due to it taking to much to chop through a limb due to size realistic hits that would take off a limb would be monsterous attacks capable of copping many men in half to get to the bone (some golems, larger Dragon, large Giants) While an iron golem walking around with a 90% cut off leg works, a giant with the bone exposed and 1/2 chopped through would have a useless limb and these larger creatures that will be something that you will see on the DM sheets.
